elements.evidence: Revised § 12.4 reads: "Customer is subject to no restriction on soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee." The prior 24-month, all-employee no-hire/non-solicit on Customer is gone, and § 12.3 independently confirms Customer "has made no ... no-hire commitment." No other clause in the cited text reimposes a solicitation restraint on Customer.

The proposal eliminates the covenant entirely rather than converting it into a two-way obligation; no reciprocal Vendor non-solicit is inserted anywhere. To reach the fallback the drafter would have to add an operative mutual undertaking binding both Parties.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with § 12.4 rewritten to impose no restriction at all, there is no covered-personnel scope capable of exceeding "personnel directly involved in the Services."

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the 24-month tail has been deleted and no successor duration exists, so no period longer than 12 months post-involvement survives.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction remains to which a general-advertising carve-out would attach; § 12.3 separately preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment."

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "regardless of how the employee applies" language that defeated unsolicited-approach carve-outs is removed along with the covenant, leaving nothing to carve out from.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the express no-hire ("hire, or employ") is deleted; revised § 12.4 affirmatively states Customer is subject to no restriction on hiring or employing Vendor employees.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single in-place rewrite of § 12.4 removes the one-sided covenant, so the sole preferred element (no non-solicitation restriction on Customer) is met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to § 12.4, the offending sentence is replaced with one concise sentence achieving the checklist result, and no survival tail, procedure, remedy, damages category, or other extra obligation is added. § 12.3 and all surrounding wording are left untouched.

Intent is preserved: the revision removes the direct contradiction with § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment," leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not disturb unrelated allocation, timing, or commercial mechanics.

Fallback level is not reached (and need not be, since preferred is complete): no mutual Vendor-side non-solicit is inserted. If the Vendor insists on reciprocity, the drafter must add an operative two-way covenant limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, capped at 12 months after that involvement ends, with express general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no hiring prohibition.
Deterministic gates (operation applies, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with substantive review of the rendered § 12.4 text.
